title: Microcks OIDC fixtures declaration
description: Source of truth for what varies in a mock OpenID Connect provider: clients, user profiles, failure paths. Mutated only through the oidc_fixtures.py subcommands. The provider identity (API name, version, issuer) is not authored here but derived from the contract, which also serves the discovery document.

declarationVersion.description: Schema version. The generator refuses a document it does not understand.

issuer.description: Value of the iss claim. Derived at init from the issuer the contract's discovery document advertises, and re-checked by verify: a relying party rejects an id_token whose iss disagrees with discovery.

api.description: Microcks API identity, derived at init from the contract's info block. Also derives the artefact file names.

signingKeyId.description: kid of the provider signing key, and the stem of its PEM files under keys/.

clock.description: Frozen timestamps. Fixed rather than computed so that rebuilding is byte-identical.

defaultProfile.description: Profile key the /authorize dispatcher falls back to when no login_hint matches. Must name a declared profile, or be null when no profile is declared.

clients.description: Declared OAuth 2.0 clients. Client ids must be unique.

id.description: client_id, and the stem of the client key files under keys/.

grant.description: authorization_code drives the browser login and mints id_tokens; client_credentials is the machine-to-machine case and mints no id_token.

auth.description: How the client authenticates at the token endpoint. private_key_jwt generates a client JWK; client_secret requires a secret.

audience.description: aud claim of the access tokens issued to this client.

scopes.description: Granted scopes. Each build also appends them to scopes_supported in the contract's discovery document, additively: nothing already advertised is ever removed.

secret.description: Required when auth is client_secret; null otherwise. Test material only.

profiles.description: User identities the mock can authenticate. Profile keys must be unique.

key.description: Identifies the profile in the declaration and derives its dispatch case name.

loginHint.description: Value of login_hint that selects this profile at the authorize endpoint.

code.description: Authorization code carrying this identity from /authorize to /token. Must be unique across profiles and error cases.

claims.description: Extra claims merged into the id_token and the userinfo response. String values and string arrays both allowed. Each build also appends the claim names to claims_supported in the contract's discovery document, additively.

errorCases.description: Rejected-login paths, each reachable through its own login_hint.

code.description: Authorization code routed to the failure response.

error.description: OAuth 2.0 error code returned by the token endpoint, for example invalid_client.
